description: Harness engineering beginner tutorial, from 0 to 1

summary.one_liner: A project-based, multilingual course that teaches how to build the environment, state management, verification, and control mechanisms that make AI coding agents work reliably.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a course (14 lectures and 8 hands-on projects) about harness engineering: the instructions, state, verification, scope, and session lifecycle around a coding agent. Lectures cover topics such as repo as source of truth, splitting instructions across files, feature lists, end-to-end verification, observability, clean handoffs, automated loops, and graph-based workflows. Projects apply these methods to a shared Electron + TypeScript + React app, with starter and solution directories per project. The repo also ships a harness-creator skill that scaffolds AGENTS.md, feature lists, init.sh, and verification workflows, plus a zero-dependency shell script (audit-harness.sh) that audits a repo against the harness subsystems. Content is available in 15 languages through a VitePress documentation site, and a build pipeline can generate PDF coursebooks.
use_cases: learn how to make coding agents reliable on real repositories
set up AGENTS.md and feature lists for a coding agent project
run a multi-session agent task without losing progress
build automated maker-checker or goal loops for agents
study harness designs of Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and DeepSeek
notable: Five-subsystem framework (instructions, state, verification, scope, session lifecycle) organizes the whole course
Projects build on each other: each project's solution becomes the next project's starter
Includes a zero-dependency shell audit script that runs without Node.js
Content translated into 15 languages, with a PDF build pipeline
Frontier harness breakdowns analyze how Pi, Claude Code, Codex, and DeepSeek build their harnesses
caveats: Requires a coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex, and the learner must let the agent edit files and run commands in real repositories
Not suited to a zero-code AI introduction; prerequisites include terminal, git, and debugging experience
Projects assume familiarity with Electron, TypeScript, and React background, which the README lists as helpful rather than required
